0.long_answer: Aspiration pneumonia is the inflammatory lung condition that frequently occurs in individuals with familial dysautonomia. These individuals often experience swallowing difficulties and episodes of vomiting due to their autonomic dysfunction. When food, liquid, or stomach contents are inadvertently inhaled into the lungs, it can lead to an infection and inflammation of the alveoli, the tiny air sacs in the lung responsible for gas exchange. This process results in aspiration pneumonia, a condition characterized by inflammation, consolidation, and sometimes suppurative (pus-forming) infections, necessitating targeted respiratory care and management.
